provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Counting 1 and 2
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count one and two objects.
The pupils should be able to trace the numbers 1 and 2.

Introduction:
We have learned to count before.
Today we will count one and two.

Content:
One is one object.
Two is two objects.
Let us pick one sweet.
Now pick two sweets.
Let us trace number 1.
Now trace number 2.

Class activity:
Each child will come and pick one or two objects from the teacher's table.

Evaluation questions:
How many pencils do I have?
Show me two fingers.
Trace number 1.

Summary:
Today we learned to count one and two objects.

topics.title: Number 3
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count three objects.
The pupils should be able to trace the number 3.

Introduction:
We have learned to count one and two.
Today we will learn about number three.

Content:
Three means three objects.
Count one, two, three fingers.
Pick three blocks from the box.\nTrace the number 3 on your slate.

Class activity:
Children will clap three times when the teacher says three.

Evaluation questions:
How many eyes do you have?
Count three books.
Trace number 3.

Summary:
Today we learned about number three.

topics.title: Number 4
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count four objects.
The pupils should be able to trace the number 4.

Introduction:
We have learned to count one, two and three.
Today we will learn about number four.

Content:
Four means four objects.
Count one, two, three, four cups.
Clap four times together.
Trace the number 4 on your slate.

Class activity:
Children will arrange four cups in a row.

Evaluation questions:
How many legs does a chair have?
Count four pencils.
Trace number 4.

Summary:
Today we learned about number four.

topics.title: Number 5
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count five objects.
The pupils should be able to trace the number 5.

Introduction:
We have learned to count up to four.
Today we will learn about number five.

Content:
Five means five objects.
Count one, two, three, four, five stones.
Jump five times like a frog.
Trace the number 5 on your slate.

Class activity:
Children will collect five stones from the playground.

Evaluation questions:
How many fingers do you have on one hand?
Count five blocks.
Trace number 5.

Summary:
Today we learned about number five.

topics.title: Counting 1 to 5
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count from 1 to 5.
The pupils should be able to match numbers to objects.

Introduction:
We have learned numbers one to five.
Today we will count them all together.

Content:
Count together from 1 to 5.
Arrange number cards from 1 to 5 in order.
Match number 1 to one object.
Match number 2 to two objects.
Do this for all numbers up to 5.

Class activity:
Children will arrange number cards 1 to 5 on the floor.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 5.
Which number comes after 3?
Match number 4 to four objects.

Summary:
Today we practiced counting from 1 to 5.

topics.title: Number 6
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count six objects.
The pupils should be able to trace the number 6.

Introduction:
We have learned to count up to five.
Today we will learn about number six.

Content:
Six means six objects.
Count six buttons on your dress.
Point to six children in the class.
Trace the number 6 on your slate.

Class activity:
Children will pass a ball around the class six times.

Evaluation questions:
How many legs does a table have?
Count six books.
Trace number 6.

Summary:
Today we learned about number six.

topics.title: Number 7
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count seven objects.
The pupils should be able to trace the number 7.

Introduction:
We have learned to count up to six.
Today we will learn about number seven.

Content:
Seven means seven objects.
Count seven leaves from the tree.
Clap seven times when I say seven.
Trace the number 7 on your slate.

Class activity:
Children will collect seven leaves from the school compound.

Evaluation questions:
How many days are in a week?
Count seven pencils.
Trace number 7.

Summary:
Today we learned about number seven.

topics.title: Number 8
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count eight objects.
The pupils should be able to trace the number 8.

Introduction:
We have learned to count up to seven.
Today we will learn about number eight.

Content:
Eight means eight objects.
Count eight crayons in your box.
Stamp your feet eight times.
Trace the number 8 on your slate.

Class activity:
Children will arrange eight crayons in a line.

Evaluation questions:
How many legs does a spider have?
Count eight blocks.
Trace number 8.

Summary:
Today we learned about number eight.

topics.title: Number 9 and 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count nine and ten objects.
The pupils should be able to trace the numbers 9 and 10.

Introduction:
We have learned to count up to eight.
Today we will learn about nine and ten.

Content:
Nine means nine objects.
Ten means ten objects.
Count nine and ten with your fingers.
Trace the number 9 on your slate.
Trace the number 10 on your slate.

Class activity:
Children will count ten fingers and ten toes.

Evaluation questions:
How many eyes do we have?
Count nine books.
Trace number 10.

Summary:
Today we learned about numbers nine and ten.

topics.title: Revision 1 to 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count from 1 to 10.
The pupils should be able to match numbers to objects.

Introduction:
We have learned numbers one to ten.
Today we will revise all of them.

Content:
Count together from 1 to 10.
Arrange number cards from 1 to 10 in order.
Count objects in the classroom like chairs and tables.

Class activity:
Children will count all the doors in the school.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 10.
Which number comes before 5?
How many windows are in our class?

Summary:
Today we revised numbers one to ten.
